title: Graph Exponential Functions
student_objective: I can graph exponential growth and decay functions and identify their intercepts, asymptotes, and end behavior.
teacher_objective: Diagnose confusion involving point generation, growth versus decay shape, y-intercepts, horizontal asymptotes, transformations, end behavior, and the fact that an exponential graph approaches but does not cross its asymptote.

concept_cards.title: Build a value table
concept_cards.content: Choose useful x-values, evaluate the function, plot the ordered pairs, and draw a smooth exponential curve.

concept_cards.title: Locate the y-intercept
concept_cards.content: For f(x)=abˣ+k, the y-intercept is (0,a+k) because b⁰=1.

concept_cards.title: Identify the asymptote
concept_cards.content: For f(x)=abˣ+k, the horizontal asymptote is y=k. The graph approaches this line without reaching it.

concept_cards.title: Recognize growth and decay
concept_cards.content: With a>0, b>1 rises from left to right; 0<b<1 falls from left to right. A negative a reflects the graph across its asymptote.

concept_cards.title: Describe end behavior
concept_cards.content: State what f(x) approaches as x moves left or right and whether the outputs increase or decrease without bound.

items.prompt: Find the y-intercept of f(x)=3(2ˣ).
items.tutor_behavior: Evaluate at x=0.

items.prompt: Does f(x)=5(0.6ˣ) show growth or decay?
items.tutor_behavior: Compare the positive base with 1.

items.prompt: State the horizontal asymptote of f(x)=4(2ˣ).
items.tutor_behavior: An unshifted exponential approaches the x-axis.

items.prompt: Find three points for y=2ˣ using x=-1, 0, 1.

solution_steps.explanation: A negative exponent gives a reciprocal.
Every nonzero base to power zero equals 1.

items.tutor_behavior: Connect each substitution to its ordered pair.

items.prompt: For g(x)=3(0.5ˣ)+2, identify the y-intercept, horizontal asymptote, and direction.

solution_steps.explanation: Evaluate at zero for the intercept.
The vertical shift is the asymptote.
The positive graph decreases from left to right.

items.tutor_behavior: Separate the intercept from the asymptote.

items.prompt: Describe the end behavior of f(x)=2(3ˣ).
items.answer_key: as x approaches negative infinity f(x) approaches 0; as x approaches infinity f(x) approaches infinity
accepted_answers: as x approaches negative infinity f(x) approaches 0; as x approaches infinity f(x) approaches infinity
left approaches 0 right rises to infinity

solution_steps.explanation: Repeated reciprocals become positive values near zero.
Repeated multiplication by 3 grows without bound.

items.tutor_behavior: Describe both ends of the graph.

items.prompt: Find the y-intercept of y=7(3ˣ).
items.tutor_behavior: Use 3⁰=1.

items.prompt: State the horizontal asymptote of y=2(4ˣ)-6.
items.tutor_behavior: Read the vertical shift k.

items.prompt: For y=(1/3)ˣ, give the point when x=-1.
items.tutor_behavior: Taking a reciprocal base to exponent -1 produces 3.

items.prompt: Classify y=4(1.2ˣ) as increasing or decreasing.
items.tutor_behavior: The base exceeds 1 and the coefficient is positive.

items.prompt: State the y-intercept and asymptote of y=5(2ˣ)+1.
items.tutor_behavior: Compute 5+1 for the intercept; use k for the asymptote.

items.prompt: Find the points on y=3(2ˣ) when x=0 and x=2.
items.tutor_behavior: Evaluate each exponent before multiplying by 3.

items.prompt: A graph has asymptote y=-4 and passes through (0,2). If its base is 2, write its equation.
items.tutor_behavior: Use 2=a-4 at x=0 to find a=6.

items.prompt: Find the y-intercept of f(x)=8(0.25ˣ).
items.tutor_behavior: The base becomes 1 at x=0.

items.prompt: State the asymptote and direction of y=4(0.7ˣ)+3.
items.tutor_behavior: Use k=3 and 0<0.7<1.

items.prompt: Find the points on y=2(3ˣ)-1 when x=0 and x=1.
items.tutor_behavior: Apply the vertical shift after multiplication.

items.prompt: Describe both ends of y=5(0.5ˣ)-2.
items.answer_key: as x approaches infinity y approaches -2; as x approaches negative infinity y approaches infinity
accepted_answers: as x approaches infinity y approaches -2; as x approaches negative infinity y approaches infinity
right approaches -2 left rises to infinity
items.tutor_behavior: Decay approaches its asymptote on the right.

items.prompt: A student draws y=2ˣ touching the x-axis at x=-4. Is that correct?
accepted_answers: no it never touches the x-axis
items.explanation_prompt: Explain why the graph cannot touch the x-axis.
items.explanation_guidance: For every real x, 2ˣ is positive. The values approach 0 as x moves left, but never equal 0, so y=0 is a horizontal asymptote.
items.tutor_behavior: Require positivity and asymptotic approach, not only the word no.

items.prompt: Find f(0) for f(x)=9(4ˣ)-2.
items.tutor_behavior: Evaluate 4⁰ first.

items.prompt: What is the asymptote of y=3(2ˣ)+8?
items.tutor_behavior: Use the vertical shift.

items.prompt: Does y=(2/5)ˣ rise or fall from left to right?
items.tutor_behavior: A positive base between 0 and 1 produces decay.

items.prompt: Find the point on y=4ˣ when x=-2.
items.tutor_behavior: Use 4⁻²=1/4².

items.prompt: Compare y=2ˣ and y=2ˣ+5. How is the second graph shifted?
items.tutor_behavior: An outside +5 raises every output.

items.prompt: Compare y=3ˣ and y=3ˣ⁻². How is the second graph shifted?
items.tutor_behavior: Subtracting 2 inside the exponent shifts right.

items.prompt: How does y=-2ˣ relate to y=2ˣ?
items.tutor_behavior: A negative outside the exponential negates all outputs.

items.prompt: Can y=3ˣ have an x-intercept?
items.tutor_behavior: The output is positive for every real x.

items.prompt: Can y=2ˣ-4 have an x-intercept? If so, state it.
items.tutor_behavior: Solve 2ˣ=4.

items.prompt: State the range of y=3(2ˣ)-7.
items.tutor_behavior: A positive coefficient keeps the graph above its asymptote.

items.prompt: State the range of y=-4(0.5ˣ)+6.
items.tutor_behavior: A negative coefficient keeps the graph below its asymptote.

items.prompt: A curve passes through (0,4), (1,8), and (2,16) and approaches y=0 on the left. Write its equation.
items.tutor_behavior: Use the y-intercept as a and the consecutive output ratio as b.

y_intercept.teacher_signal: Does not evaluate the function at x=0

horizontal_asymptote.teacher_signal: Confuses the asymptote with an intercept

shifted_features.teacher_signal: Cannot coordinate intercept, asymptote, and direction

end_behavior.teacher_signal: Reverses or omits one end of the graph

features_to_equation.teacher_signal: Cannot recover an equation from graph features

asymptote_crossing.teacher_signal: Draws an exponential graph touching its asymptote

reflection.teacher_signal: Does not identify reflection across the asymptote

x_intercept.teacher_signal: Assumes every exponential has or lacks an x-intercept

range_from_graph.teacher_signal: Includes the asymptote in the range or chooses the wrong side

graph_to_equation.teacher_signal: Cannot infer coefficient and base from plotted points
